Now speaking

Morning, George — it's Monday the twenty-fourth, and today's one to respect the heat: Athens is under a red-code fire alert, with the city pushing thirty-seven degrees and the low forties inland.

Abroad it's heavy — the US is set to drop its next round of Iran sanctions today, and it's Ukraine's Independence Day, with Kyiv braced for Russia to mark it with something big.

— personal items —

Let's start with Iran, where the pressure keeps ratcheting.

Washington says it'll roll out another round of economic measures today, hitting Iran and anyone still trading with it — the batch Tehran's already branded a declaration of war on every nation that deals with it.

The naval blockade has all but choked off Iran's oil; even China, its biggest buyer, has cut imports sharply, and the IMF now sees inflation nearing seventy percent by year's end.

This is the squeeze phase, so keep half an eye on it.

Then Ukraine, marking its Independence Day under threat.

Kyiv's been warned Russia may dip into its missile reserves for a big strike on the capital's power grid, and it already hit the city with ballistic missiles overnight.

But the war cuts both ways: Ukraine's long drone campaign on Russian refineries has bitten so hard that fuel queues are forming in Moscow itself for the first time, and the Kremlin's finally admitting the shortage.

For your science hit: researchers used AI to crack a long-standing puzzle — the genetic switch that tells a gene to turn on.

After training on around half a million DNA sequences, the model pinpointed that starter signal in roughly sixty percent of human genes, which could sharpen everything from disease research to designing better therapies.

Over in AI, the very top of the leaderboard's quiet again — no new flagship overnight, and Claude Opus five still sits at number one.

The move worth knowing is Google's: it's rolled out Gemini three-point-seven Flash, a cheaper, faster model aimed squarely at coding, document work, and business automation, with introductory pricing running through the end of the year.

If you're wiring AI into the app, it's worth a look as the low-cost workhorse tier — the kind of thing you reach for on high-volume, straightforward calls rather than your hardest reasoning.

Athens today is punishing: clear and bone-dry, around twenty-seven early, a high near thirty-seven in the afternoon, easing only into the low thirties by evening.

The bigger deal is that red-code fire alert across Attica — the top warning level — so steer well clear of anything that could spark, especially outdoors.

Strong northerly meltemi winds will push through, gusty near the coast, and sunset's at eighteen past eight.

Your own patch is light today.

— personal items —

Health-wise, in this kind of dry, forty-degree heat you sweat more than you notice, so keep a bottle close and drink before you're thirsty, especially if you're anywhere near the wall today.

And to leave you a touch sharper.

Word of the day: crimp — in climbing, gripping a tiny edge with just your fingertips, knuckles bent, sometimes thumb clamped over the top for extra power; brutally strong, but hard on the tendons, so ease into it.

And a productivity trick worth stealing: eat the frog — do your single most important or most dreaded task first thing, before the day fills up with everything else.

Clear that one and the rest feels downhill.

That's your Monday — fire-alert hot at home, heavy news abroad, and a quiet, unhurried day for you.

Drink water, mind the heat, and take it slow.
